title: Magnetotransport of tomographic electrons in a Corbino disk
abstract: In clean electron gases at low-to-moderate temperatures, odd-parity modes of the Fermi surface are anomalously long-lived due to Pauli blocking, giving rise to ``tomographic transport'' that is not captured by a hydrodynamic model. Here we show that tomographic flow in a Corbino disk induces an extended boundary layer near electrodes with superballistic transport and enhanced slip velocity, which leads to a parametric enhancement of the quadratic magnetoresistance coefficient. The enhancement depends explicitly on the electrode curvature, allowing its strength to be controlled by the device geometry. The magnetoresistance coefficient reveals three distinct regimes as a function of magnetic field: a tomographic regime at weak fields; a hydrodynamic regime at intermediate fields, reached when the cyclotron radius becomes comparable to a large odd-mode mean free path; and a conventional Ohmic regime at large fields, reached when the cyclotron radius becomes comparable to the short even-mode mean free path. The tomographic regime is characterized by an anomalous dependence of the magnetoresistance on temperature and density, which may account for recent experimentally observed anomalous scaling of the electron viscosity.
summary: This work develops a kinetic theory framework to describe magnetotransport in electron gases within a Corbino disk. It identifies 'tomographic transport' as an anomaly arising from long-lived odd-parity Fermi surface modes, which modifies standard hydrodynamic predictions. The resulting theoretical description predicts distinct crossover regimes for magnetoresistance dependent on the magnetic field strength.
main_problem: The study addresses 'tomographic transport' in clean electron gases, an anomalous transport mechanism not captured by standard hydrodynamic models.
main_result: Tomographic flow induces superballistic current injection at electrodes and enhances the magnetoresistance coefficient, which exhibits a non-monotonic dependence on magnetic field strength across three distinct regimes.
method: The analysis employs matched asymptotic expansions of the kinetic equation, distinguishing between bulk behavior and near-electrode boundary layers.
model_or_system: The system is an electron gas confined in a Corbino disk geometry. The theory models quasiparticle distribution functions using Fermi-liquid equations linearized around equilibrium.
key_observables: Magnetoresistance coefficient, azimuthal velocity profile u_theta(r), and electrode conductance G_e.
important_parameters: Odd-mode mean free path (l_o), even-mode mean free path (l_e), cyclotron radius (r_c), and the ratio of these lengths to device size L.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on systematic expansions in Knudsen numbers ($k_e, k_o$) and assumes that tomographic corrections are responsible for observed anomalous scaling.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate schematic transport paths showing boundary layers, profiles of velocity and potential across different magnetic field regimes (tomographic, hydrodynamic, Ohmic), and the non-monotonic dependence of magnetoresistance curvature on $1/r_c$.
paper_structure: The paper builds from the general kinetic equation by linearizing it and expanding in Knudsen numbers. It then solves for the bulk flow using matched asymptotic expansions, incorporating specific boundary conditions at the electrodes to derive corrections to transport coefficients like viscosity.
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter transport, the use of non-equilibrium statistical mechanics (kinetic theory) and the derivation of anomalous scaling laws provide rigorous theoretical tools applicable to understanding far-from-equilibrium dynamics in quantum systems.
